title: Selective Injection of Tracer into Rat Gastric Mucosa and Muscle
author: John Furness

steps.title: Prepare Animal and Operating Area
steps.instruction: Prepare Sprague Dawley rats (200-500 g, both sexes) that have been fasted overnight.

substeps.instruction: Place rat on a warm (30 °C) operating table under aseptic conditions.
Clip fur from the upper abdomen.
Swab the area with chlorhexidine followed by 70% ethanol.
Cover the area with sterile protective film (Opsite Flexigrid TM).
Protect eyes from drying using Lacrilube.

steps.title: Administer Anesthesia and Analgesia
steps.instruction: Administer required medications prior to surgery.

substeps.instruction: Inject carprofen (5 mg/kg) subcutaneously as an analgesic.
Inject a mixture of medetomidine (0.5 mg/kg) and ketamine (75 mg/kg) intraperitoneally using a 27 gauge needle.

steps.title: Expose the Stomach
steps.instruction: Surgically open the abdominal cavity to access the stomach.

substeps.instruction: Open the skin and abdominal muscle in the mid-line, from the xyphoid process caudally for 1.5 cm, separately.
Exteriorize the stomach and keep it constantly moist with physiological saline.

steps.title: Inject Neuronal Tracers
steps.instruction: Inject neuronal tracers (e.g., Retrobeads TM) into the gastric tissue using beveled glass micropipettes (tip diameter 60-90 µm) disinfected in 70% ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Inject 30-100 nL volumes at multiple sites.
For gastric muscle (antrum, corpus, or fundus): Introduce micropipette at a low angle (~10 degrees) to the level of the myenteric plexus.
For pyloric sphincter muscle: Advance the tip into the constricted region between the stomach and duodenum, avoiding and preserving blood vessels.

For mucosa: Open the stomach along the greater curvature from the gastric groove to the antrum, remove gastric content with cotton buds, partly evert the stomach, and insert micropipettes into the mucosa at a low angle of approach, monitoring visually under a surgical microscope.

steps.title: Close Surgical Incisions
steps.instruction: Close the surgical site in reverse order.

substeps.instruction: Close the stomach incision with sterile 5.0 (USP) silk suture.
Close the abdominal wall with sterile 2.0 (USP) polydioxanone absorbable suture.
Close the skin incision with surgical staples.

steps.title: Post-Operative Recovery
steps.instruction: Manage the animal's recovery and reversal of anesthesia.

substeps.instruction: Reverse anesthesia by administering atipamezole hydrochloride (1 mg/kg) intraperitoneally.
Monitor rats visually during recovery (approx. 1.5-2 h).
Return to animal holding room and monitor daily.

steps.title: Tissue Harvesting and Perfusion
steps.instruction: Harvest tissues 7 to 14 days after tracer injection.

substeps.instruction: Deeply anesthetize animals with pentobarbital sodium.
Confirm anesthesia via lack of response to vigorous skin pinch.
Perfuse via cardiac puncture with phosphate buffered saline followed by 4% paraformaldehyde.
Remove nodose ganglia and stomach; place in 4% paraformaldehyde overnight.
Wash tissues 3x 10 minutes in PBS.

steps.title: Process and Image Nodose Ganglia
steps.instruction: Prepare and image the nodose ganglia using confocal microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Dissect nodose ganglia to remove all connective tissue.
Place on microscope slides with fluorescence mounting medium (Dako) and cover-slip with slight compression.
Image using a confocal fluorescence microscope (Zeiss LSM800 Airyscan) using large tile scans at various focal planes (z-stack) in red and green channels.
Identify labeled neurons and determine cell body area size using Zen Blue 3.0 software (Zeiss).

steps.title: Process and Image Stomach Injection Sites
steps.instruction: Document and analyze the tracer injection sites in the stomach.

substeps.instruction: Photograph injection sites and store tissue in PBS/0.1% sodium azide.
For thick tissue imaging: Dissect out injection sites, mount on slides in rubber-tape constructed wells, cover-slip, and scan at low power using confocal microscopy.

For cryosectioning: Place specimens in 30% sucrose in PBS overnight, then in a 50:50 mixture of 30% sucrose/PBS and Optimal cutting temperature (OCT) compound overnight, then place in cryomolds with 100% OCT compound and freeze using iso-pentane cooled in liquid nitrogen.
Cut sections (20-30 µm thick) using a Cryostat, mount on slides, and image on a fluorescence microscope (Zeiss Axio-observer/Zeiss HRMc) with a color camera.
